key_insight: In lock-exchange flow with a bubble curtain, the previously broad breakthrough regime actually splits into three distinct subregimes, controlled by both air Froude number and the salt-to-fresh water density ratio.
engineering_relevance: For ship-lock design, bubble-curtain performance cannot be tuned using air Froude number alone; the density contrast of the water layers materially changes how well salt transport is blocked.
method: Two-phase large-eddy simulations of a laboratory-scale lock-exchange setup
Detailed analysis of flow and density fields around the bubble curtain
Regime classification based on hydrodynamic response and transport blocking
evidence_signal: The abstract reports simulation-based evidence showing three qualitatively distinct subregimes and a corresponding dependence of salt-blocking effectiveness on the density ratio.
watch_item: Results are from laboratory-scale LES, so practical optimization should account for scale effects and real lock conditions before direct deployment.
paper_title: Lock-exchange flow regimes under low air Froude number bubble curtains
